claim: Neurons regulate their excitability by adjusting their ion channel levels.
source: Neurons regulate their excitability by adjusting their ion channel levels.
evidence: This is a well-established concept in neuroscience supported by multiple citations in the manuscript.

claim: Degeneracy facilitates regulation by enabling a disruptive change in one channel to be offset by compensatory changes in other channels.
source: Degeneracy – achieving equivalent outcomes (excitability) using different solutions (channel combinations) – facilitates this regulation by enabling a disruptive change in one channel to be offset by compensatory changes in other channels.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Pleiotropy complicates regulation because a compensatory ion channel change that restores one property to its target value often disrupts other properties.
source: Pleiotropy – the impact of one channel on more than one property – complicates regulation because a compensatory ion channel change that restores one property to its target value often disrupts other properties.
evidence: This is a central claim of the manuscript, demonstrated through experiments and modeling.

claim: Properties can be effectively coregulated only if the number of adjustable channels (nin) exceeds the number of regulated properties (nout).
source: Properties can be effectively coregulated only if the number of adjustable channels (nin) exceeds the number of regulated properties (nout).
evidence: This is a main finding demonstrated through computational modeling in the manuscript.

claim: Ion channel correlations emerge during homeostatic regulation when the dimensionality of solution space (nin − nout) is low.
source: Ion channel correlations emerge during homeostatic regulation when the dimensionality of solution space (nin − nout) is low.
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational simulations shown in Figures 6-8.

claim: Regulation as a whole fails if single-output solution sets do not intersect.
source: Even if each property can be regulated to its target value when considered in isolation, regulation as a whole fails if single-output solution sets do not intersect.
evidence: This is demonstrated through modeling results shown in Figures 9 and 10.

claim: Ion channels must be coadjusted with different ratios to regulate different properties.
source: Our results also highlight that ion channels must be coadjusted with different ratios to regulate different properties, which suggests that each error signal drives modulatory changes independently, despite those changes ultimately affecting the same ion channels.
evidence: This is inferred from the modeling results and discussed in the context of feedback control mechanisms.

claim: Neurons maintain their average firing rate near a target value by adjusting their intrinsic excitability and synaptic weights.
source: Neurons maintain their average firing rate near a target value, or set point, by adjusting their intrinsic excitability and synaptic weights (Turrigiano et al., 1994; O'Leary et al., 2010; Aizenman et al., 2003; Desai et al., 1999; Hengen et al., 2013; van Welie et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies.

claim: Homeostatic regulation of intrinsic excitability is achieved through feedback control of diverse ion channels.
source: Homeostatic regulation of intrinsic excitability is achieved through feedback control of diverse ion channels (Turrigiano et al., 1994; O'Leary et al., 2010; Desai et al., 1999; Joseph and Turrigiano, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental and theoretical studies.

claim: Different ion channel combinations can produce equivalent excitability.
source: Firing rate homeostasis is facilitated by the ability of different ion channel combinations to produce equivalent excitability (Marder, 2011).
evidence: This is a well-established concept in neuroscience supported by citations.

claim: Blocking native IM with 10 μM XE991 caused depolarization in CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: Membrane potential differed across conditions (F3,16 = 298.49, p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA); specifically, it was depolarized by blocking IM (t = 18.71, p < 0.001, Tukey test)
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Blocking native IM caused spike amplitude attenuation in CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: Spike amplitude also differed across conditions (F3,16 = 154.04, p < 0.001); specifically, it was attenuated by blocking IM (t = 20.23, p < 0.001)
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Blocking native IM increased firing rate in CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: Firing rate also differed across conditions (F3,16 = 177.61, p < 0.001); specifically, it was increased by blocking IM (t = 18.38, p < 0.001)
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Inserting virtual IM reversed the depolarization caused by blocking native IM.
source: Inserting virtual IM or virtual IAHP reversed the depolarization (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Inserting virtual IAHP reversed the depolarization caused by blocking native IM.
source: Inserting virtual IM or virtual IAHP reversed the depolarization (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Inserting virtual IM reversed the spike amplitude attenuation caused by blocking native IM.
source: Inserting virtual IM or virtual IAHP reversed the depolarization (Figure 2C), spike amplitude attenuation (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Inserting virtual IAHP reversed the spike amplitude attenuation caused by blocking native IM.
source: Inserting virtual IM or virtual IAHP reversed the depolarization (Figure 2C), spike amplitude attenuation (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Inserting virtual IM reversed the firing rate increase caused by blocking native IM.
source: Inserting virtual IM or virtual IAHP reversed the depolarization (Figure 2C), spike amplitude attenuation (Figure 2D), and firing rate increase (Figure 2E) caused by blocking native IM.
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Inserting virtual IAHP reversed the firing rate increase caused by blocking native IM.
source: Inserting virtual IM or virtual IAHP reversed the depolarization (Figure 2C), spike amplitude attenuation (Figure 2D), and firing rate increase (Figure 2E) caused by blocking native IM.
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Replacing native IM with virtual IM did not affect firing pattern (CVISI).
source: Replacing native IM with virtual IM did not affect firing pattern, quantified as the coefficient of variation of the interspike interval (CVISI)
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Virtual IAHP reduced CVISI compared to native or virtual IM.
source: whereas virtual IAHP reduced CVISI (Figure 2F)
evidence: This is directly measured experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Virtual IAHP caused the neuron to spike at different times than the neuron with native or virtual IM.
source: often causing the neuron to spike at different times (in response to different stimulus fluctuations) than the neuron with native or virtual IM (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is directly observed experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Ion channel density combinations that produce the target value for one property yield differing values for other properties.
source: We began by testing whether ion channel density combinations that produce the target value for one property also produce a consistent value for other properties.
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 3.

claim: Density combinations yielding the same rheobase did not yield the same minimum sustainable firing rate (fmin).
source: Despite yielding the same rheobase, density combinations along the a–b contour did not yield the same minimum sustainable firing rate (fmin) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Density combinations yielding the same rheobase did not yield equivalent stimulation-evoked firing rates.
source: Density combinations yielding the same rheobase did not yield equivalent stimulation-evoked firing rates (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Energy consumption rate increased with firing rate but did not increase equivalently across all density combinations.
source: Energy consumption rate increased with firing rate, as expected, but did not increase equivalently across all density combinations, as evident from the variation in energy consumption rate along the iso-firing rate contour (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Density combinations yielding equally efficient spikes yielded different stimulation-evoked firing rates and rheobase values.
source: Density combinations yielding equally efficient spikes yielded different stimulation-evoked firing rates and rheobase values (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 3H.

claim: The multioutput solution set for firing rate and energy efficiency corresponds to where the two single-output solution sets intersect.
source: The multioutput solution set for firing rate and energy efficiency (nout = 2) corresponds to where the two single-output solution sets intersect, which occurs at a point – only one density combination yields the target values for both properties, meaning the multioutput solution is unique.
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 5A.

claim: When nin = 3, many density combinations yield the target values for both properties, meaning the multioutput solution is degenerate.
source: But if another conductance like gleak is adjustable (nin = 3), the curves in 2D parameter space (top panel) transform into surfaces in 3D parameter space (bottom panel) and those surfaces intersect along a curve – many density combinations yield the target values for both properties, meaning the multioutput solution is degenerate.
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Robust regulation of n properties requires >n adjustable ion channels even if each ion channel contributes to regulation of >1 property.
source: From this, we conclude that robust regulation of n properties requires >n adjustable ion channels even if each ion channel contributes to regulation of >1 property.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figure 5.

claim: The dimensionality of solution space affects ion channel correlations by limiting the degrees of freedom.
source: We predicted that the dimensionality of solution space – point (0D), curve (1D), surface (2D), volume (3D), etc. – affects ion channel correlations by limiting the degrees of freedom.
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figures 6-8.

claim: When firing rate and energy efficiency are both regulated with nin = 3, solutions converge on a curve and pairwise correlations strengthen.
source: However, if firing rate and energy efficiency are both regulated (nout = 2; Figure 6D), homeostatically determined solutions are once again constrained to fall along a curve when nin = 3, and pairwise correlations strengthen (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 6E.

claim: When firing rate and energy efficiency are both regulated, correlations strengthen and become independent of the relative regulation rates.
source: However, if firing rate and energy efficiency are both homeostatically regulated, correlations strengthen (consistent with results from Figure 6) and become independent of the relative regulation rates because solutions are limited to a lower-dimensional solution space (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Noise causes solutions to spread across the available solution space.
source: After a few hundred noise-update iterations, solutions spread across the available solution space, which corresponds to a surface when only firing rate is regulated (Figure 8A, top).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 8A.

claim: When firing rate and energy efficiency were regulated, noise caused solutions to spread across the intersection but correlations were relatively unaffected.
source: When firing rate and energy efficiency were regulated, noise caused solutions to spread across the intersection (Figure 8C) but correlations were relatively unaffected since they are limited by the low dimensionality of this solution space.
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Coadjusting ḡNa, ḡK, and ḡM can successfully regulate energy efficiency.
source: Figure 9B shows successful regulation of energy efficiency by coadjusting the same three channels.
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Using the same initial conditions and relative regulation rates, the system failed to coregulate firing rate and energy efficiency.
source: Using the same initial conditions and relative regulation rates as above, the system failed to coregulate firing rate and energy efficiency (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Ion channel correlations increase as single-output solution sets start to disconnect.
source: By converging on the intersection, which is a curve, ion channel correlations are stronger than in Figure 10A. In other words, ion channel correlations increase as single-output solution sets start to disconnect, meaning increased correlations presage regulation failure
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Coregulation of multiple properties is incompatible with the amalgamation of error signals.
source: The analogy with single- and multiobjective optimization (see above) seems apropos. Critically, nin exceeding nout will not guarantee solutions if degrees of freedom are reduced by bottlenecks elsewhere in the feedback loops.
evidence: This is inferred from the modeling results and discussed in the context of feedback control mechanisms.

claim: Neurons might take advantage of regulating as many properties as their ion channel diversity safely allows, leading to a relatively low-dimensional solution space.
source: Though nout is constrained by nin (i.e., the number of regulated properties cannot exceed the number of adjustable ion channels), neurons might take advantage of regulating as many properties as their ion channel diversity safely allows, leading to a relatively low-dimensional solution space (as nout approaches nin).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the modeling results.

claim: A multioutput solution set can be empty because single-output solution sets do not intersect.
source: A multioutput solution set can be empty because single-output solution sets do not intersect (Figure 10C), meaning regulation of different properties to their respective target values is incompatible.
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Regulation can fail because negative feedback fails to converge on available solutions.
source: Regulation can also fail because negative feedback fails to converge on available solutions (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figure 9C.

claim: A multioutput solution set may become less accessible as single-output solution sets start to separate.
source: Notably, a multioutput solution set may become less accessible (lower dimensional) as single-output solution sets start to separate (Figure 10B), and may foreshadow the eventual disjunction of those solution sets (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through computational modeling shown in Figures 10B and 10C.

claim: Neurons can coregulate multiple properties by coadjusting ion channels.
source: In conclusion, neurons can coregulate multiple properties by coadjusting ion channels.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript based on experimental and modeling results.

claim: Many channels are required to coregulate many properties despite reusing channels to regulate more than one property.
source: Despite reusing channels to regulate more than one property, many channels are required to coregulate many properties and feedback loops must allow for coadjustments with different ratios.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the manuscript based on modeling results.

claim: Feedback loops must allow for coadjustments with different ratios to coregulate multiple properties.
source: Despite reusing channels to regulate more than one property, many channels are required to coregulate many properties and feedback loops must allow for coadjustments with different ratios.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the manuscript based on modeling results.

claim: The value of fmin reflects spike initiation dynamics: fmin >> 0 spk/s is consistent with class 2 excitability and operation as a coincidence detector.
source: The value of fmin reflects spike initiation dynamics: fmin >> 0 spk/s is consistent with class 2 excitability (Hodgkin, 1948) and operation as a coincidence detector (Ratté et al., 2014a)
evidence: This is based on established knowledge and citations.

claim: fmin≈ 0 spk/s is consistent with class 1 excitability and operation as an integrator.
source: whereas fmin≈ 0 spk/s is consistent with class 1 excitability and operation as an integrator
evidence: This is based on established knowledge.

claim: Spikes are energetically costly but vary in their energy efficiency based on the temporal overlap in sodium and potassium channel activation.
source: Spikes are energetically costly (Attwell and Laughlin, 2001) but vary in their energy efficiency based on the temporal overlap in sodium and potassium channel activation (Sengupta et al., 2010; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Energy efficiency decreases propagation safety factor.
source: but energy efficiency decreases propagation safety factor (Al-Basha and Prescott, 2019)
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: A target value for energy efficiency likely emerges by balancing competing interests.
source: and a target value likely emerges by balancing these competing interests (Speakman et al., 2011).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning supported by a citation.

claim: Degeneracy is synonymous with underdetermination.
source: Degeneracy is synonymous with underdetermination, which highlights that degeneracy depends not only on ion channel diversity, but also on those channels not having to coregulate 'too many' properties.
evidence: This is an inference based on the analogy with systems of linear equations.

claim: Extra degrees of freedom broaden the range of available solutions.
source: Extra degrees of freedom broaden the range of available solutions, meaning a good solution is liable to exist over a broader range of conditions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mathematical framework.

claim: If constraints outnumber the degrees of freedom, the system becomes overdetermined and solutions disappear.
source: On the other hand, if constraints outnumber the degrees of freedom, the system becomes overdetermined and solutions disappear (e.g., Figure 5D), which can cause regulation to fail (see below).
evidence: This is an inference based on the mathematical framework and demonstrated in Figure 5D.

claim: Ion channel diversity has been selected for because it enables the addition of new functionality without the cell becoming overdetermined.
source: One might reasonably speculate that ion channel diversity has been selected for because it enables the addition of new functionality (e.g., excitability) without the cell becoming overdetermined, lest pre-existing functions (e.g., osmoregulation) become compromised.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the modeling results.

claim: Fitting a model with n parameters to many outputs is more difficult but yields better parameter estimates than fitting the same model to just one output.
source: Fitting a model with n parameters to many outputs (e.g., firing rate and input resistance and rheobase and spike height) is more difficult but yields better parameter estimates than fitting the same model to just one output (Foster et al., 1993)
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Degeneracy makes solving the inverse problem difficult, if not impossible.
source: Degeneracy makes solving this inverse problem difficult, if not impossible (Sarkar and Sobie, 2010; Aster et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: A neuron does not solve an inverse problem because it does not regulate its conductance densities to particular values.
source: A neuron needs to regulate its properties but does not do so by regulating its conductance densities to particular values; in that respect, a neuron does not solve an inverse problem.
evidence: This is an inference based on the modeling results and discussion.

claim: Neurons have evolved under selective pressure to be degenerate, not parsimonious.
source: Neurons have evolved under selective pressure to be degenerate (see above), not parsimonious, contrary to how most models are constructed.
evidence: This is an inference based on the modeling results and evolutionary reasoning.

claim: Coregulating many properties using a common set of ion channels is feasible only if enough different channels are involved.
source: Our results show that coregulating many properties using a common set of ion channels is feasible only if enough different channels are involved.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the manuscript based on modeling results.

claim: For coadjustments to work, channels must differ from each other in how they affect each property.
source: Indeed, for coadjustments to work, channels must differ from each other in how they affect each property (see Figure 1), which emphasizes the distinction between degeneracy and redundancy.
evidence: This is an inference based on the modeling results and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Regulation of each property requires that ion channels are coadjusted with different ratios, which necessitates separate master regulators.
source: Our results also highlight the need for >1 'master regulator' because regulation of each property requires that ion channels are coadjusted with different ratios (Figure 11).
evidence: This is an inference based on the modeling results and illustrated in Figure 11.

claim: Local or kinetically distinct variations in calcium could encode >1 error signal if the calcium sensors are spatially segregated or operate with different filter properties.
source: But local (Bootman et al., 2001) or kinetically distinct (Liu et al., 1998) variations in calcium could encode >1 error signal if the calcium sensors coupling intracellular calcium to gene expression or channel modulation are spatially segregated or operate with different filter properties.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning supported by citations.

claim: Firing rate homeostasis can be activity independent, use membrane potential as feedback, or involve dual feedback loops.
source: Beyond calcium, evidence points to firing rate homeostasis being activity independent (MacLean et al., 2003), using membrane potential as feedback (Santin and Schulz, 2019), or involving dual feedback loops (Kulik et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to experimental studies.

claim: The AMP:ATP ratio is used to track energy level.
source: Furthermore, the AMP:ATP ratio is used to track energy level (Hardie, 2014; Garcia and Shaw, 2017)
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Free amino acids can be sensed by cells.
source: and free amino acids can also be sensed (Efeyan et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: mTOR is modulated by diverse factors and modulates many processes including transcription, translation and protein degradation.
source: Take mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) for example; it is modulated by diverse factors and, in turn, modulates many processes including transcription, translation and protein degradation (Switon et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Coregulation of multiple properties is incompatible with certain control steps.
source: The analogy with single- and multiobjective optimization (see above) seems apropos. Critically, nin exceeding nout will not guarantee solutions if degrees of freedom are reduced by bottlenecks elsewhere in the feedback loops.
evidence: This is an inference based on the modeling results.

claim: The existence of pairwise correlations suggests that the dimensionality of solution space (=nin − nout) is relatively low.
source: Notwithstanding molecular interactions, the existence of pairwise correlations suggests that the dimensionality of solution space (=nin − nout) is relatively low.
evidence: This is an inference based on the modeling results.

claim: Failed homeostatic regulation may have similar consequence regardless of how the failure occurs.
source: Failed homeostatic regulation may have similar consequence regardless of how the failure occurs, consistent with the emergence of common disease phenotypes despite vastly different underlying pathologies (Ramocki and Zoghbi, 2008)
evidence: This is speculative reasoning supported by a citation.

claim: Subtle differences in exactly how regulation failure transpires may provide important clues to help pinpoint the underlying mechanism(s).
source: but subtle differences in exactly how the failure transpires may provide important clues to help pinpoint the underlying mechanism(s).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning.

claim: Evolution has yielded diverse channels and complicated transcriptional regulation to enable coregulation of multiple properties.
source: This may account for why evolution has yielded such diverse channels and why their transcriptional regulation has become so complicated (Gabel et al., 2015).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning supported by a citation.

claim: Accounting for the coregulation of multiple properties may be crucial for appreciating design features that might otherwise elude us.
source: But if that is indeed the case, then accounting for the coregulation of multiple properties may be crucial for appreciating design features that might otherwise elude us.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the overall findings.
